answer.rationale: The 18% mandate requires material cost reduction. Memory_c2 shows switching vendors achieved sharp unit cost cuts with low onboarding friction. Memory_c6 shows multi-year commitments with incumbent unlock volume pricing. Verification of both positions informs whether to renegotiate with incumbent (leveraging c6's precedent that longer commitments reduce unit cost) or validate that a switch remains viable (c2's proof point). Negotiate_terms is chosen because: (1) it addresses the cost mandate directly by reopening pricing discussions with incumbent, (2) it preserves the stable integration documented in memory_c1, (3) it avoids the 14-day cliff by engaging now, and (4) competitive pressure from c2's success gives negotiating leverage. The 94% volume buffer is tight—negotiate_terms carries lower onboarding risk than switch_primary_vendor. Standard_experiment scale means structuring negotiation to include trial pricing/terms before full commitment, preserving exit options if the incumbent cannot meet the 18% target. Downstream risk flagged because failure to secure cost reduction forces emergency switching with compressed timeline. Uncertainty preserved by not assuming incumbent will move on price (enables pivot to switch_primary_vendor in next cycle if negotiation fails).
